BBC News (Iain Watson, Political correspondent) — published Thursday 24 September 2026 23:44 BST (metadata cXenseParse:publishtime 2026-09-24T23:44:38Z)

HEADLINE: New policies, election speculation: What to expect from Burnham's first Labour conference as PM

KEY VERIFIED FACTS:
- Labour's annual conference is in LIVERPOOL. Burnham takes to the stage on TUESDAY (29 September) for his debut leader's speech. Conference slogan this year: "Hope Again".
- An internal No 10 note has set out the broad themes he will explore, including setting out long-term solutions to build a belief that the future can be brighter.
- He is likely to point to his forthcoming 10 Year Plan for the UK, which he says will have "making life more affordable" at its core.
- Policy announcements are promised on EACH DAY of the conference, starting on SATURDAY (26 September). Each will fit the PM's priorities: "putting power in people's hands" (more devolved powers); "growth in every postcode"; and help with cost of living.
- Party insiders say measures such as REMOVING VAT FROM ELECTRICITY BILLS are "just the start of that assistance".
- John Healey delivers his first conference speech as chancellor on MONDAY (28 September). Borrowing costs for last month soared to their second highest level; he will not scoop his own Budget next month.
- A potential crowd-pleaser: telling activists he will set up a commission to examine electoral reform — supported by about a quarter of his own MPs.
- Conclusions of the review by former Labour cabinet minister Alan Milburn on getting young people into work or training are likely to be published soon.
- Unite, Labour's biggest union funder, wants robust action on living costs. Its leader Sharon Graham has called for a "winter fuel in reverse". Unite's motion offers options including a cap on energy prices and unfreezing tax thresholds. Unite says revenue can be raised through a windfall tax on banks. The TUC has called for an increase in the bank surcharge to subsidise energy bills.
- POLLING: Labour has moved from just under 20% at the end of the Starmer era to around the mid-twenties. Ipsos puts Labour as high as 28%; YouGov registers 23%. Reform UK's share is 21% in YouGov, its lowest since January 2025, now neck-and-neck with the Conservatives. Labour is still well below the 34% vote share it won in 2024.
- New YouGov research suggests that at constituency level, 63-68% of Lib Dem and Green voters would tactically vote Labour to stop Reform UK winning their seat.
- Burnham does not have to call an election until AUGUST 2029. Party HQ has recently launched "operation second term". Downing Street insists an early election is not being planned.
- Holborn and St Pancras by-election takes place a week after conference concludes.
- Possible conference flashpoints: a push by some on the left for a complete ban on arms sales to Israel and for Labour to describe Israel's actions in Gaza as genocide; proposals to make migrants wait much longer for permanent residency; and whether the Rosebank and Jackdaw oil and gas fields should go ahead.

QUOTE (Andy Burnham, to reporters en route to the UN General Assembly, reported by BBC): "People are going to know the direction I want to take this country and I will set it down quite clearly."
QUOTE (Andy Burnham, on his debut leader's speech): it would leave nobody in any doubt about "what I'm trying to do in this role".
QUOTE (Senior Labour officials, per BBC): the conference is an opportunity to "show voters a party that is boldly, confidently, and authentically Labour".
